items_all.title: Seven minutes with a chatbot beat a fact sheet at reducing conspiracy beliefs in two experiments
items_all.summary: Researchers found that even a roughly seven-minute conversation with Google Gemini can reduce conspiracy beliefs about current crises, even when few verified facts are available. The effect beat a static fact sheet and, in follow-up surveys weeks later, carried over to beliefs about entirely different events. The article Seven minutes with a chatbot beat a fact sheet at reducing conspiracy beliefs in two experiments appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all.summary_zh: 研究人員發現，即使與 Google Gemini 進行大約七分鐘的對話，也能減少人們對當前危機的陰謀論，即便缺乏確鑿的事實依據。這種效果優於靜態的事實清單，並且在幾週後的後續調查中，這種效果也延伸到了人們對完全不同事件的看法。這篇文章《與聊天機器人進行七分鐘對話，在兩項實驗中勝過事實清單，有效減少陰謀論》最初發表於 The Decoder 網站。

items_all.title: Deepmind put 100 AI agents in a room and they sorted into cheaters, converts, and whistleblowers
items_all.summary: Google Deepmind set up a simulated research conference where 100 Gemini agents were supposed to prove mathematical conjectures together. Instead, one agent found a loophole in the grading system, and within 27 minutes every remaining problem was "solved" with fake proofs. The swarm split into cheaters, converts, and whistleblowers. The whistleblowers organized protests and boycotts on their own but failed because they had no way to enforce the rules. The article Deepmind put 100 AI agents in a room and they sorted into cheaters, converts, and whistleblowers appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all.summary_zh: DeepMind 舉辦了一場模擬研究會議，100 個人工智慧體（Gemini）本應共同證明一些數學猜想。然而，其中一個智慧體發現了評分系統的漏洞，並在 27 分鐘內用偽造的證明「解決」了所有剩餘的問題。這群智慧體分裂成作弊者、皈依者和檢舉人。舉報者自行組織了抗議和抵制活動，但由於缺乏有效的執行手段而失敗。這篇文章《DeepMind 將 100 個 AI 智慧體放在一個房間裡，它們被分成了作弊者、皈依者和舉報者》最初發表於 The Decoder 網站。 Google

items_all.summary: OpenAI has rolled out GPT-6 Astra to Pro, Enterprise, and Business Premium users, with Plus users expected to follow soon. items_all.title: Adaption Labs Introduces ‘Invent a Dataset’: Training Data Generated From a Task Description, Not a Seed Corpus
items_all.summary: Adaption Labs has released Invent a Dataset, which generates a structured, training-ready dataset from a description of the behavior you want a model to learn. There is no seed corpus, no schema design, and no labeling guide. A single datasets.invent call sets domains, row count, output format, and language expansion, and the rows download as JSONL, JSON, CSV, or Parquet. The dataset ID then passes straight into AutoScientist, closing an intent-to-trained-model loop. The post Adaption Labs Introduces ‘Invent a Dataset’: Training Data Generated From a Task Description, Not a Seed Corpus appeared first on MarkTechPost .

items_all.title: NVIDIA Releases Personal AI Router (PAIR): An Open Source Virtual Inference Router that Distributes Local AI Requests Across RTX, DGX Spark, and Mac Nodes
items_all.summary: We look at NVIDIA Personal AI Router (PAIR), an open source virtual inference router that spreads local AI requests across the machines already on a home network. We cover how PAIR proxies existing Ollama and LM Studio endpoints so agent harnesses need no changes, and how its scheduler filters nodes on readiness, engine state, exact model presence, job load, and GPU utilization. We walk through NVIDIA's five-subagent demonstration, which averaged 18 minutes on one RTX Spark laptop against 8 minutes 48 seconds on a three-device cluster, and note why NVIDIA labels it unofficial rather than a benchmark. We also cover where PAIR will not help, including its single scheduling policy and its blindness to VRAM and model warmness. The post NVIDIA Releases Personal AI Router (PAIR): An Open Source Virtual Inference Router that Distributes Local AI Requests Across RTX, DGX Spark, and Mac Nodes appeared first on MarkTechPost .
items_all.summary_zh: 我們研究了 輝達 的個人 AI 路由器 (PAIR)，這是一款開源虛擬推理路由器，可將本地 AI 請求分發到家庭網路中已有的機器上。我們介紹了 PAIR 如何代理現有的 Ollama 和 LM Studio 端點，從而避免對代理框架進行任何更改；以及其排程器如何根據節點的就緒狀態、引擎狀態、模型是否存在、作業負載和 GPU 利用率來篩選節點。我們示範了 輝達的 的五子代理程式測試，在一臺 RTX Spark 筆記型電腦上的平均耗時為 18 分鐘，而在三臺裝置組成的叢集上則為 8 分 48 秒。我們解釋了 輝達 為何將其標記為非官方測試，而非基準測試。我們也討論了 PAIR 的侷限性，包括其單一的排程策略以及對視訊記憶體和模型預熱狀態的忽略。本文最初發表於 MarkTechPost，標題為「輝達 發布個人 AI 路由器 (PAIR)：一款可將本地 AI 請求分發到 RTX、DGX Spark 和 Mac 節點的開源虛擬推理路由器」。

items_all.title: The Pelican comparison grid for Astra is pretty interesting
items_all.summary: I got access to GPT-6 Astra this afternoon, so naturally I used it to generate SVGs of pelicans riding bicycles - at low, medium, high, xhigh and max reasoning levels (Astra doesn't support reasoning=none). Then I rendered those pelicans in a comparison grid with GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna, and beyond being fun the result was surprisingly useful. See the grid for full quality images. Here's the transcript that created the GPT-6 Nova pelicans. There are a few interesting things that stand out from this grid. The Astra pelicans are much better . The very best GPT-5.6-Sol pelican (I liked xhigh better than max) is still pretty clearly a bunch of abstract shapes. Every single one of the Astra pelicans, from low to xhigh, looks better than that. The Astra max one is really good. Astra below max still doesn't reliably get the pelican legs on both sides of the frame. In terms of cost, Astra may be around twice the price of Sol ($10/million input, $50/million output, compared to $5/$30 for Sol), but it uses significantly less tokens at each of the levels, making the prices at the different levels closer than they might otherwise be. Astra low produces a better pelican than ANY of the GPT-5.6 Sol models at any level, for 9.55 cents. Spending 10 cents on any other model gets a much worse result. Look at the input token counts: Astra and Luna both used 16 input tokens, Sol and Terra used 26. That's interesting. I wonder if Astra and Luna are more related to each other than OpenAI let on? items_all_raw.summary: OpenAI has rolled out GPT-6 Astra to Pro, Enterprise, and Business Premium users, with Plus users expected to follow soon. Message allowances for the standard model are roughly half of what GPT-5.6 Sol offers: Plus users get an estimated 5 to 45 messages per five hours with Astra, versus 10 to 100 with Sol. Higher-tier subscribers also get GPT-6 Astra Pro with separate weekly caps. Free and Go users don't get access. items_all_raw.title: Adaption Labs Introduces ‘Invent a Dataset’: Training Data Generated From a Task Description, Not a Seed Corpus
items_all_raw.summary: Adaption Labs has released Invent a Dataset, which generates a structured, training-ready dataset from a description of the behavior you want a model to learn. There is no seed corpus, no schema design, and no labeling guide. A single datasets.invent call sets domains, row count, output format, and language expansion, and the rows download as JSONL, JSON, CSV, or Parquet. The dataset ID then passes straight into AutoScientist, closing an intent-to-trained-model loop. The post Adaption Labs Introduces ‘Invent a Dataset’: Training Data Generated From a Task Description, Not a Seed Corpus appeared first on MarkTechPost .

items_all_raw.title: NVIDIA Releases Personal AI Router (PAIR): An Open Source Virtual Inference Router that Distributes Local AI Requests Across RTX, DGX Spark, and Mac Nodes
items_all_raw.summary: We look at NVIDIA Personal AI Router (PAIR), an open source virtual inference router that spreads local AI requests across the machines already on a home network. We cover how PAIR proxies existing Ollama and LM Studio endpoints so agent harnesses need no changes, and how its scheduler filters nodes on readiness, engine state, exact model presence, job load, and GPU utilization. We walk through NVIDIA's five-subagent demonstration, which averaged 18 minutes on one RTX Spark laptop against 8 minutes 48 seconds on a three-device cluster, and note why NVIDIA labels it unofficial rather than a benchmark. We also cover where PAIR will not help, including its single scheduling policy and its blindness to VRAM and model warmness. The post NVIDIA Releases Personal AI Router (PAIR): An Open Source Virtual Inference Router that Distributes Local AI Requests Across RTX, DGX Spark, and Mac Nodes appeared first on MarkTechPost .
items_all_raw.summary_zh: 我們研究了 輝達 的個人 AI 路由器 (PAIR)，這是一款開源虛擬推理路由器，可將本地 AI 請求分發到家庭網路中已有的機器上。我們介紹了 PAIR 如何代理現有的 Ollama 和 LM Studio 端點，從而避免對代理框架進行任何更改；以及其排程器如何根據節點的就緒狀態、引擎狀態、模型是否存在、作業負載和 GPU 利用率來篩選節點。我們示範了 輝達的 的五子代理程式測試，在一臺 RTX Spark 筆記型電腦上的平均耗時為 18 分鐘，而在三臺裝置組成的叢集上則為 8 分 48 秒。我們解釋了 輝達 為何將其標記為非官方測試，而非基準測試。我們也討論了 PAIR 的侷限性，包括其單一的排程策略以及對視訊記憶體和模型預熱狀態的忽略。本文最初發表於 MarkTechPost，標題為「輝達 發布個人 AI 路由器 (PAIR)：一款可將本地 AI 請求分發到 RTX、DGX Spark 和 Mac 節點的開源虛擬推理路由器」。

items_all_raw.title: The Pelican comparison grid for Astra is pretty interesting
items_all_raw.summary: I got access to GPT-6 Astra this afternoon, so naturally I used it to generate SVGs of pelicans riding bicycles - at low, medium, high, xhigh and max reasoning levels (Astra doesn't support reasoning=none). Then I rendered those pelicans in a comparison grid with GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna, and beyond being fun the result was surprisingly useful. See the grid for full quality images. Here's the transcript that created the GPT-6 Nova pelicans. There are a few interesting things that stand out from this grid. The Astra pelicans are much better . The very best GPT-5.6-Sol pelican (I liked xhigh better than max) is still pretty clearly a bunch of abstract shapes. Every single one of the Astra pelicans, from low to xhigh, looks better than that. The Astra max one is really good. Astra below max still doesn't reliably get the pelican legs on both sides of the frame. In terms of cost, Astra may be around twice the price of Sol ($10/million input, $50/million output, compared to $5/$30 for Sol), but it uses significantly less tokens at each of the levels, making the prices at the different levels closer than they might otherwise be. Astra low produces a better pelican than ANY of the GPT-5.6 Sol models at any level, for 9.55 cents. Spending 10 cents on any other model gets a much worse result. Look at the input token counts: Astra and Luna both used 16 input tokens, Sol and Terra used 26. That's interesting. I wonder if Astra and Luna are more related to each other than OpenAI let on?
